newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom expands reliance on Astra.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom expands reliance on Astra.

text.p: German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG said on Friday it had decided not to launch its own satellites to replace its DFS-Kopernikus equipment but to rely more heavily on the Astra satellite network.

Societe Europeenne des Satellites S.A., (SES) the Luxembourg-based company that operates the Astra network, said in a separate release that with the launch of its Astra2B satellite it would operate capacity on behalf of Telekom.
The satellite would transmit television and radio, distribute television programming to cable television networks and corporate television services as well as satellite news gathering.
"This decision allows us to use existing synergies and to further strengthen our position in the market," said Gerd Tenzer, Telekom board member in charge of technology.
The Astra 2B satellite will be launched during the autumn of 1998 and will be deployed at the orbital location 28.2 degrees east, replacing Kopernikus which is located at 28.5 degrees east, SES said.
The Astra 2B will operate an FSS bandwidth of 250 Megahertz between 12.50 and 12.75 Gigahertz.
A second satellite that Astra will have at this orbital location will provide digital direct-to-home services in Europe, particularly to the United Kingdom and Ireland.
The Kopernikus programme precedes the Astra network, which is Europe's leading direct-to-satellite broadcast network.
A Telekom spokesman said the Kopernikus spacecraft would remain in operation "well beyond 1998" but after the deployment of Astra 2B would only serve as backup.
Telekom holds a 16.7 percent stake in SES and also holds a stake of 8.1 percent in Eutelsat, a competing satellite network owned by state telecoms companies.
Telekom said it would also expand its relationship with Eutelsat, but did not elaborate.
